Open Start and type your company name and your own numbers in the yellow cells: your lowest margin, the margin you want, the minimum order, the grace days for an invoice, the late fee and the yearly cost of waiting for money.

Wholesale accounts lists the shops you sell to (selling to shops at about half the retail price) with the terms, the tier and the minimum order. The orders, sales, last order, usual gap, open invoices and reorder check fill in.

Wholesale orders and Wholesale lines hold each order and its products. The total, the cost of goods, the margin (profit as a share of the price) and the minimum check fill in, and the maker and the packer get a ready message.

Wholesale invoices and Payments received follow the money. Only open invoices turn late, after the grace days; the days to pay and the oldest late invoice are on the dashboard. Credit notes and Returns and credits record what you gave back.

Line sheet is the price and product list you give a shop, with the wholesale price, the retail price, the minimum pack and the margin for the shop. Price tiers and Terms options hold the discounts and the early payment discount.
Sample requests, Shop calls and visits, Account notes, Prospects and Catalogue requests keep the selling work: what you sent, who you talked to, what the shop said and which prospect is next.

Reorder reminders turns the usual gap between orders into the next expected order of each shop and product, so you call before a shop forgets you. Account sales by month gives the sales and the margin of each shop.
Wholesale shipments records the boxes, the weight, the courier cost and the days to deliver, and shows the freight as a share of the order.

Use the 14 calculators before you decide: price, margin, minimum order, tier discount, late fee, early payment, account profit, reorder date, sample payback, freight, credit note, cash by week, rounding and a what-if grid.

Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to open a chat with the text already written (28 messages). Check your own local rules for sales tax, invoices and credit notes.
Read the Wholesale Shops and Invoices sheet and the Charts every week: open and late invoices, payments, shops overdue to reorder, samples and prospects.

The 24 products with margin, sales and rating
One row for each product with price, cost, status and since date; the margin, age, sales and profit of the last 12 months, units, rating and checks fill in from the other sheets.
Units, revenue and costs by product, month and channel
One row for each product, month and channel with units, revenue and the costs; the total cost, margin and margin share fill in, and every chart of sales reads this sheet.
Customer reviews with rating, topic and reply time
One row for each review with the rating, topic and the day you replied; the days to reply, the reply check and the customer phone fill in so none is forgotten.
What each review topic means and the rating you want
The review topics with a plain meaning and the rating you want on each; the Reviews sheet and the topic chart use these.
New product ideas from first thought to launch
One row for each idea with its stage, source, owner and the expected price and cost; the expected margin, the days in the pipeline and the margin check fill in.
Trial batches with sell-through and tester scores
One row for each trial batch with the units made and sold, the tester score and the decision; the sell-through, days since the start and the targets check fill in.
Campaigns with spend, orders, revenue and return
One row for each campaign with the spend, the orders and the revenue; the return on spend, the profit after spend and the result fill in.
Campaign orders and revenue by week
One row for each campaign week with the orders, the revenue and the new customers; the campaign name, the average order and the share of new customers fill in.
Customers with orders, spend and months since the last order
One row for each customer with the first and last order, the orders and the spend; the months since the last order, the average order and the customer check fill in.
New customers by first order month and repeat orders
One row for each first order month with the customers and those who ordered again; the repeat share and the age of the cohort fill in.
Units to make in each month of the coming year
One row for each month with the demand factor and the day to finish planning; last year's units, the units from the factor, the units to make and the plan check fill in.
Seasonal gift sets with price, cost and margin
One row for each gift set with the occasion, the contents, the price and the cost; the margin, the profit on one set and the days to launch fill in.
Prices of similar products from other sellers
One row for each product you saw from another seller with the price and the size; the price for 100 g, the same for your range and the price check fill in.
Photo shoots with cost and photos used
One row for each photo shoot with the products, the photos taken and used and the cost; the cost for each product, the share used and the check fill in.
Newsletters with opens, orders and revenue
One row for each newsletter with the topic, the recipients, the opens, the orders and the revenue; the open rate, the order rate, the revenue for each 1,000 sent and the check fill in.
Customers waiting for a product to come back
One row for each customer who asked to hear when a product is back, with the day they joined and the day you told them; the days waiting, the check and the phone fill in.
What testers said about samples of new products
One row for each tester answer with the scent score, the look score and a comment; the average score, the check and the tester phone fill in.
Products to keep, reprice or retire
One row for each product you reviewed with the units and margin you saw and your decision; the live units, the live margin and the retire check fill in.
The five sales channels with fee and payout days
The channels you sell through with the fee each keeps and the days until you are paid; the product month sheet reads the channel names.
